subject.title: File Browser: Remove ALLOWED_FILE_NAMES whitelist, add scope levels

question: Should OpenClaw approve workspace-wide editing and/or host-filesystem browsing in Mission Control, and what permission boundary should replace the current bootstrap-file allowlist?
rationale: The remaining request changes which files trusted operator clients can read or mutate, while current main deliberately separates read-only workspace browsing from allowlisted bootstrap-file edits.

options.title: Approve workspace-only path first
options.body: Use the current read-only `agents.workspace.*` contract as the base, review the canonical workspace-management work for scoped CRUD, and defer host-filesystem access.

options.title: Keep bootstrap edits only
options.body: Leave Mission Control editing restricted to bootstrap and memory files while read-only workspace previews remain the only broader file surface.

options.title: Design system scope separately
options.body: Open a separate security design for host-filesystem browsing with explicit opt-in, read/write limits, auditing, and recovery UX before implementation.

recommendation.title: Approve workspace-only path first
recommendation.body: Use the current read-only `agents.workspace.*` contract as the base, review the canonical workspace-management work for scoped CRUD, and defer host-filesystem access.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently owned the read-only workspace boundary and related mobile workspace file-browser rollout while deferring mutations to the broader design thread.
